claims.explanation: Erlotinib is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor whose selectivity is driven primarily by activating EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions and L858R) that create constitutive, drug-sensitive EGFR signaling; EGFR-mutant lines such as HCC4006, NCIH1650, and KYSE270 are among the most killed, while EGFR-wild-type lines with alternative MAPK/PI3K drivers (BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, PTEN loss) are largely spared. Co-occurring resistance mechanisms such as MET amplification or downstream pathway activation (KRAS/BRAF/NRAS mutations, PTEN loss) blunt erlotinib response and are protective.

features.basis: Activating exon 19 deletion/L858R mutations predict erlotinib response in NSCLC (EURTAC, OPTIMAL, never-smoker sequencing); EGFR-mutant lines HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270 are top killed.
EGFR dependency/expression is required for erlotinib sensitivity; EGFR-driven lines are selectively killed.
MET amplification drives ERBB3/PI3K-mediated gefitinib/erlotinib resistance.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling and are associated with primary EGFR-TKI resistance; KRAS-mutant lines (OV7, SNU410, CL11, T3M4) are spared.
BRAF mutations bypass EGFR dependence and predict poor EGFR-TKI response; BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines are least affected.
NRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK and confer EGFR-TKI resistance; NRAS-mutant lines (KU1919, IPC298) are spared.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT independent of EGFR, reducing erlotinib sensitivity; PTEN-mutant lines (786O, KALS1, UACC62, FTC133) are least affected.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K downstream of EGFR and can blunt EGFR-TKI response.
ERBB3 (HER3)-dependent PI3K activation mediates MET-driven erlotinib resistance.
NR1I2 (PXR) is an annotated erlotinib target and can modulate drug metabolism/resistance.
TP53 mutation is common in both killed and spared lines and does not explain selectivity; weak evidence.
CDKN2A loss appears in several spared lines but is not mechanistically linked to EGFR-TKI response; weak evidence.
